designPrinciples: Root-cause, generalized fix - never hardcoded to the $50m/$25m illustration or to any specific covenant family pair. Every mechanism below operates over the same open, generic FAMILY_KEYWORDS taxonomy and a purely numeric/text-grammar value-anchor extractor - zero package-, company-, or covenant-specific keyword lists (Architecture Invariants #29).

GROUNDED, never raw-AI-paraphrase-hashed: this task's own explicit prohibition. Every new identity input is either (a) real, deterministic SOURCE TEXT itself (the semantic-coverage layer operates purely on real document text, no LLM involved at all), or (b) a candidate-supplied value/quote INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED present in the real source text before being trusted for anything (the discovery layer, which does see LLM-authored `description`/`distinguishingQuote` fields). An unverified AI claim is discarded, never used as a partial/weak signal - fail-closed, matching this codebase's own established discipline (e.g. Phase 1A's exact-resolution-only relativeRef policy).

Formatting-invariant by construction: every numeric value is canonicalized (comma/whitespace/multiplier-word stripped, parsed to a plain number) before comparison, and every quote match is whitespace-normalized before substring-checking - two differently-formatted renderings of the identical real value/text always produce the identical anchor.

Never turns a genuine duplicate into a false-distinct sibling: two independently-worded re-detections of the SAME real clause normalize to the SAME grounded anchor set regardless of paraphrase wording (adversarial case 8), because the anchor is the underlying VALUE/verbatim-quote, never the wording that carries it.

Graceful, disclosed degradation - never a crash, never a silently-wrong identity. When no source-grounded disambiguating signal exists at all (no differing verified number, no verified quote), identity falls back to exactly the pre-existing (already-disclosed) V1 behavior for that pair - a strict superset of remediation, never a regression.

sharedUtility.purpose: New, generic, package-agnostic module shared identically by both identity layers (discovery/pass-c-neighborhood.ts and semantic-coverage/unit-hypothesis.ts) - reused, not duplicated, so 'these two claims are distinct' can never diverge between layers merely because they extracted numbers differently.
functions: extractValueAnchors(text): currency/percentage/ratio value extraction via generic regex grammar (no covenant keywords), canonicalized to tagged anchor strings ('usd:50000000', 'pct:5', 'ratio:3') - '$50,000,000', '$50 million', and '$50MM' all normalize identically.
valueAnchorSetsDisjointAndNonEmpty(a, b): true only when both sides carry at least one anchor AND share none - the genuine-numeric-difference test used by the coverage-layer splitter.

extractGroundedValueAnchors(candidateText, sourceGroundTruthText): extracts anchors from (possibly AI-authored) candidateText but keeps only those independently confirmed present in the real source ground truth - the GROUNDING discipline that lets the discovery layer safely use Pass B's own `description` field without hashing raw paraphrase.

verifyDistinguishingQuote(quote, sourceGroundTruthText): whitespace-normalized verbatim-substring verification with a minimum non-trivial length (12 non-whitespace chars) to reject generic-word false positives - returns the normalized quote (safe to use for identity) only when verified, else null.

discoveryLayer.newFingerprintFormula: computeCandidateContentFingerprint(c) = [familyPart, valuePart, quotePart].join('|') where familyPart = sorted(dedupe(families)).join(','), valuePart = sorted(dedupe(valueAnchors)).join(','), quotePart = verifiedQuoteFingerprint ?? ''. Folded into BOTH discoveryId and pass-d-reconcile.ts's mergeKey, exactly as the V1 fix already established (so 'these merge' and 'these get the same discoveryId' can never diverge).

dimension1_groundedDescriptionValues.mechanism: For every ExpandedCandidate, extractGroundedValueAnchors(item.description, anchorNode's real full OWN text) - extracts numeric/currency/percentage/ratio values from the candidate's own (possibly AI-authored) description, keeping only values independently verified present in the real source text of the resolved anchor node.
dimension1_groundedDescriptionValues.whyThisClosesTheMotivatingExample: Pass B's prompt already instructs 'Emit one WireRule per independently operative rule - never merge distinct baskets into one' (semantic/prompt.ts) and the ORIGINAL certification's own part3_confirmedNewFinding F15-1 already confirmed Pass B's OWN detection is correct (2 distinct items, 2 distinct descriptions) even in the collision case - the defect was always purely in downstream identity derivation, never detection. A real $50m/$25m basket pair's own descriptions virtually always name their own dollar figure (that IS what makes them distinct, real, differently-sized covenant baskets) - grounding those figures against the shared source node's real text (which contains BOTH figures) yields two disjoint, verified anchor sets with zero Pass B schema or prompt dependency.
dimension1_groundedDescriptionValues.groundingDiscipline: A hallucinated or mis-paraphrased number that does not actually appear in the source is silently dropped, never trusted (verified by a direct unit test in tests/contract-model/claim-identity-v2.test.ts).

dimension2_verifiedDistinguishingQuote.mechanism: OPTIONAL, tolerant Pass B wire-schema extension: `distinguishingQuote` (a short verbatim excerpt, <=200 chars in the prompt guidance, capped to 240 chars on ingestion). pass-c-neighborhood.ts verifies it via verifyDistinguishingQuote against the anchor node's real full text; when verified, the normalized quote becomes `verifiedQuoteFingerprint` and any value anchors WITHIN the quote are folded into `valueAnchors` too.
dimension2_verifiedDistinguishingQuote.passBChanges: WireSemanticRuleItemSchema gained the optional field; SYSTEM_PROMPT gained one new instruction sentence (DISTINGUISHING QUOTE); DISCOVERY_PROMPT_VERSION bumped v2 -> v3 (a real contract change per this file's own established bump discipline).
dimension2_verifiedDistinguishingQuote.toleranceAndGenerality: Never covenant/section-specific - the instruction is entirely generic ('when this section bundles two or more independently operative rules into ONE un-enumerated sentence... give distinguishingQuote for EACH'). An absent, empty, or unverifiable quote degrades gracefully to whatever dimension-1 (grounded description values) already contributes - never a crash, never a silently wrong identity.
dimension2_verifiedDistinguishingQuote.honestLimitation: This dimension's real-world effectiveness for a NON-numeric distinguishing case (e.g. 'Revolving Facility' vs 'Term Facility', no dollar figures at all) depends on Pass B (a live LLM call) actually following the new prompt instruction. This session has no configured LLM API key (the same disclosed constraint 13-claim-identity-certification.json's own part3_confirmedNewFinding F15-1 and this phase's Workstream H both already carry) - so this dimension's live-prompt-compliance rate is NOT independently verified here, only its VERIFICATION mechanics (a supplied quote is exercised and correctly split/rejected via direct construction of SemanticRuleItem objects, matching every prior claim-identity test file's own established discipline of bypassing the LLM boundary and constructing Pass B's OUTPUT shape directly).

discoveryLayer.mergeAndPropagation: pass-d-reconcile.ts unions valueAnchors on a genuine-duplicate merge (mirroring its existing mergedNodeKeys/mergedMethods/mergedSignals union pattern) and keeps whichever verifiedQuoteFingerprint exists. Both new fields are exposed as OPTIONAL fields on DiscoveredCandidate itself (never hidden only inside the opaque discoveryId hash) so a downstream reviewer can see exactly why two same-family/role/node candidates were kept distinct - consistent with this codebase's own disclosure discipline elsewhere (supersessionReason, roleNormalizationStatus, etc). Optional (not required) specifically so pre-existing ExpandedCandidate/DiscoveredCandidate test-fixture literals across the repo (grep-confirmed 26 files reference DiscoveredCandidate) continue to type-check unmodified.
discoveryLayer.versionBump: DISCOVERY_PIPELINE_VERSION v3 -> v4 (identity-formula change, per this constant's own established bump discipline) and DISCOVERY_PROMPT_VERSION v2 -> v3 (wire schema + prompt change).

semanticCoverageLayer.mechanism: findCoordinateClauseSplit's existing cross-family trigger is UNCHANGED (regression-safe). A NEW same-family trigger is added: when both sides of a top-level 'and'/'or' independently match the SAME family keyword (not different), the split now ALSO fires when valueAnchorSetsDisjointAndNonEmpty(extractValueAnchors(leftText), extractValueAnchors(rightText)) is true - i.e. each side independently states a numeric/currency/percentage/ratio value AND the two values genuinely differ.
semanticCoverageLayer.whyThisIsStronglyGeneral: This layer is FULLY deterministic (semantic-coverage's own Independence Contract forbids any LLM/discovery/conclusion-module dependency, mechanically enforced by tests/contract-model/semantic-coverage-independence.test.ts) - the fix requires ZERO model cooperation and is therefore an unconditional, always-active closure of the numeric-anchored same-family case, not merely an opt-in improvement. This is the PREFERRED identity source per safe-failure/identity.ts's own documented precedence (`su:` semanticUnitId preferred over `cr:` candidateRef fallback), so the strongest, most model-independent half of this fix lives exactly where the codebase already says identity should be trusted first.
regressionGuards: Same family, no number on either side ('shall not create or suffer to exist any Lien... except Permitted Liens') - never splits (no anchor to compare).
Same family, IDENTICAL value on both sides (a clause restating its own single cap) - never splits (sets are not disjoint).
Right clause restates a modal verb ('...and shall not permit...') - never splits, regardless of family/value (pre-existing guard, unchanged).
semanticCoverageLayer.versionBump: SEMANTIC_COVERAGE_ALGORITHM_VERSION v3 -> v4 (detection-algorithm change, per this constant's own established bump discipline).

No existing caller, test, or persisted shape is broken by its addition (confirmed: full tsc/eslint/test suite run below).

Per this task's own explicit instruction ('you're allowed to extend its normalized output in a TOLERANT, GENERAL way'), a minimal, optional, verified-before-trusted extension was the correct, smallest-blast-radius way to give the discovery layer a chance to close that narrower residual too, without inventing a second identity mechanism or hardcoding any covenant-specific rule.

disclosedResidual.severity: MINOR (disclosed, not silently hidden - matches this phase's own and the prior phase's disclosure discipline)
disclosedResidual.title: Two genuinely distinct, same-family, same-role, same-source-node claims fused in one un-enumerated sentence STILL collide when NEITHER side states any numeric/currency/percentage/ratio value AND Pass B does not supply a distinguishingQuote that independently verifies against the real source text
disclosedResidual.example: 'The Company shall not incur Indebtedness under the Revolving Facility or incur Indebtedness under the Term Facility.' - both clauses are INDEBTEDNESS family, neither states a number, and (in this session's necessarily-LLM-free test construction) no distinguishingQuote was supplied.
whyThisIsMaterially-narrowerThanBefore: Before this workstream: ANY same-family fused pair collided (RESIDUAL-1 in 11-claim-identity-remediation.json), including the exact $50m/$25m motivating example.

After this workstream: the collision now requires the ADDITIONAL, simultaneous absence of (a) any independently-verifiable numeric value differential on either side, AND (b) a Pass-B-supplied, source-verified distinguishing quote. A real covenant basket that is economically meaningful virtually always states its own dollar figure or percentage - that IS what typically makes two baskets distinct in the first place. A purely name-based distinction with zero numeric content anywhere is a materially rarer real-drafting shape than the general defect class AUDIT-F4 froze.
disclosedResidual.whyNotFullyClosed: No field on SemanticRuleItem or the semantic-coverage layer's own deterministic text scan is simultaneously (a) source-grounded, (b) free of raw-AI-paraphrase-hashing risk, (c) free of ordinal/position instability, and (d) capable of splitting two same-family, zero-number, zero-model-cooperation claims. Fully closing this would require either mandatory (not optional) Pass B quote compliance verified against a live model - unverifiable in this environment (no configured LLM API key, the same disclosed constraint every predecessor claim-identity artifact in this codebase already carries) - or a materially larger, more aggressive text-similarity/embedding-based mechanism explicitly out of scope for a deterministic, non-package-specific fix.
disclosedResidual.coveredByTest: tests/contract-model/claim-identity-blocker8-remediation.test.ts's 'AUDIT-F4 STILL-OPEN (undisclosed by Pass B)' test - asserts and documents the current (still-merged) behavior explicitly for this exact narrower shape, immediately followed by two RESOLVED tests proving the SAME fused sentence splits correctly the moment either a numeric value or a verified quote is available - so the boundary of what remains open is precisely pinned down in CI, not left vague.
mitigatingFactors: Every mitigating factor 11-claim-identity-remediation.json's own part4_disclosedResidualRisk already named for the BROADER pre-V2 residual still applies unchanged: multipleRulesLikely disclosure, the semantic compiler's own multi-rule prompt recovering both claims from full operativeSourceText at compile time (live-model-dependent, unverified this session per the same disclosed constraint), coverage-layer reconciliation matching by compiled-rule citation rather than candidateRef, and the safe-failure verification gate remaining conservative (an unresolved MATERIAL finding under either sub-claim still fails the whole merged candidateRef - this residual can under-credit, never falsely over-credit, a genuinely correct claim).

The semantic-coverage layer (semanticUnitId, the PREFERRED identity source) now has NO remaining residual for the numeric-anchored case at all, and only this narrower zero-number sub-case remains open there too - a strict improvement over the pre-V2 state where EVERY same-family fusion collided regardless of numeric content.
